{{Short description|Austrian mathematician and computer scientist (1964–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} 
[[File:GerhardWoeginger 2011 MFO14972.jpg|thumb|Woeginger at the [[Combinatorial Optimization]] Workshop 2011 in [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]]]]
'''Gerhard J. Woeginger''' (31 May 1964 – 1 April 2022) was an Austrian mathematician and computer scientist who worked in Germany as a professor at [[RWTH Aachen University]], where he chaired the algorithms and complexity group in the department of computer science.<ref>{{citation|url=http://algo.rwth-aachen.de|title=Algorithmen und Komplexität|language=de|publisher=RWTH|access-date=26 October 2023}}.</ref>

== Biography ==
Woeginger was born on 31 May 1964 in [[Graz]], Austria. He obtained a diploma from the [[Graz University of Technology]] (TU Graz) in 1987,<ref name="ae"/> and completed his Ph.D. at TU Graz 1991 under the supervision of Franz Rendl.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=56410}}</ref> He worked on the faculty of TU Graz from 1991 to 2001, where he completed his [[habilitation]] in 1995. He then moved to the [[University of Twente]] from 2001 to 2004, to [[Eindhoven University of Technology|TU Eindhoven]],<ref name="ae"/> from 2004 to 2016, and finally to [[RWTH Aachen]] in 2016.

He was program chair of the [[European Symposium on Algorithms]] in 1997, of the algorithms track of the [[International Colloquium on Automata, Languages and Programming]] in 2003, of the [[European Conference on Operational Research]] in 2009, and of several other conferences.

In 1996, Woeginger won the [[Start-Preis]], the highest Austrian award for scientists under the age of&nbsp;35.<ref>{{citation|url=http://list.fwf.ac.at/de/wissenschaft-konkret/im-fokus-start/starter-liste/1996|title=Die START-ProjektleiterInnen im Portrait: Jahrgang 1996|language=de|publisher=[[Austrian Science Fund]]|access-date=19 September 2015|archive-date=29 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160529174022/http://list.fwf.ac.at/de/wissenschaft-konkret/im-fokus-start/starter-liste/1996|url-status=dead}}.</ref> He won a [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award]] in 2011.<ref name=lenstra/>
In 2014, he was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref name="ae">{{citation|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Woeginger_Gerhard/CV|title=Gerhard Woeginger - Biography|publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]|access-date=18 September 2015}}.</ref>

Until September 2016, Woeginger maintained a list of attempts to settle the [[P versus NP problem]] on his website.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.win.tue.nl/~wscor/woeginger/P-versus-NP.htm|title=The P-versus-NP page|publisher=Gerhard Woeginger|access-date=26 October 2023}}.</ref><ref name=lenstra>{{cite journal |last1=Lenstra |first1=Jan Karl |last2=Rendl |first2=Franz |last3=Spieksma |first3=Frits |last4=Uetz |first4=Marc |date=11 September 2022 |title=In memoriam Gerhard Woeginger |journal=Journal of Scheduling |volume=25 |issue=5 |pages=503–505 |doi=10.1007/s10951-022-00748-4 |doi-access=free }}</ref> As of its last update, the list tallied 116 attempts dating back to 1986 to settle the question in various ways.

Woeginger died on 1 April 2022, at the age of 57.<ref>{{citation|url=https://algo.rwth-aachen.de/ |title=Algorithmen und Komplexität Startseite |language=de |trans-title=Algorithms and Complexity Home Page |publisher=RWTH Aachen, Lehrstuhl für Informatik 1 – Algorithmen und Komplexität |access-date=4 April 2022 |quote=Am 1. April ist Prof. Gerhard Woeginger im Alter von 57 Jahren nach schwerer Krankheit überraschend verstorben. |trans-quote=On 1 April, Prof. Gerhard Woeginger died suddenly after a severe illness at the age of 57.}}</ref>
